originality.rationale: The closest primary full text, Benedetti--Lutz Theorem 6.3, only supplies an existence witness for non-evasiveness beginning at vertex 3. Requiring all fourteen roots and counting exactly 122 admissible two-step prefixes is strictly stronger, not implied by that witness or by vertex-decomposability theorems (Rudin is not vertex-decomposable). Resultary finds the same evaluated record, which is excluded as independent prior art, and a separate eight-vertex-ball root result, which is not a general domination. Hachimori and Macaulay2 exact-object pages provide facets and global properties, not this profile. No published prior statement implying this exact classification was identified after actual full-text inspection of the closest theorem. Best-of-knowledge qualified PASS, not priority certification.

value.rationale: Rudin’s non-shellable, non-vertex-decomposable yet non-evasive 3-ball is a classic computational/topological test case. Whether all vertices may initiate a recursive non-evasiveness proof is a natural robustness invariant directly related to the property distinguishing this object. The exact multiset (11^6,9^4,5^4) and 122 admissible ordered first-two queries quantify the earliest loss of uniform choice. The finite classification is exact for a standard object, not an arbitrary unmotivated small slice; no general theorem or downstream paper-sized consequence is claimed.
